text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The five-nation committee monitoring ceasefire in Lebanon held a prolonged meeting due to a complaint filed by Lebanon after a Lebanese woman was killed by Israeli shelling in the south on Tuesday.
-Security forces arrested an Iraqi citizen suspected of being involved in assassination operations against Iraqi opposition figures outside Lebanon.
-Japan demanded that Lebanon hand over six members of the Japanese Red Army who were arrested in Beirut and the Bekaa valley.
-The state-owned Lebanese University teachers will go on a two-day long strike on March 4 to protest against the university administration's delay in implementing some academic decisions.
-The World Bank granted Lebanon a $53-million loan to rehabilitate its water grid.
-Israeli forces kidnapped a Lebanese shepherd and shelled wide areas in south Lebanon.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir headed to Vatican to participate in the Synod meeting for Asia.
-Austria's Foreign Minister will arrive in Beirut today on a three-day visit to discuss with Lebanese top officials bilateral relations and the regional situation.
-Head of the political department of the PLO Kaddoumi discussed with Foreign Minister Bouez the situation of Palestinian refugees in Lebanon.
